notes: Replaced shield-automatic-mitigation-web-acl-rule-group with shield-health-based-unhealthy-mitigation-threshold because AWS has announced retirement of the former feature on January 29, 2027 ([AWS retirement notice](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/aws-shield-advanced-is-embracing-the-aws-waf-anti-ddos-managed-rule-group-what-changes-and-how-to-prepare/)). Replaced dns-firewall-fail-open-forwarding with dns-firewall-default-failure-enforcement and direct-connect-macsec-must-encrypt-failure with direct-connect-last-ckn-enforcement-reversion to avoid answers inferable from setting names.

cards.statement: An Amazon EBS snapshot can capture an EC2 instance's RAM for a forensic investigation.
cards.explanation: An EBS snapshot captures volume data. Responders need a separate memory acquisition to preserve volatile RAM evidence.
cards.misconception: A disk snapshot also captures the running instance's memory.

source.title: AWS Security Incident Response Guide: Collect and analyze forensic evidence

cards.statement: A responder who stops an EBS-backed EC2 instance erases forensic data on its instance store volumes.
cards.explanation: Stopping an EBS-backed EC2 instance erases its instance store data. Responders need to acquire relevant local-disk artifacts before stopping it.

source.title: Stop and start Amazon EC2 instances

cards.statement: EC2 termination protection blocks an intruder's OS shutdown when instance shutdown behavior is terminate.
cards.explanation: DisableApiTermination protects against EC2 API termination. An OS-initiated shutdown still terminates the instance when InstanceInitiatedShutdownBehavior is terminate.
cards.misconception: API termination protection also prevents termination initiated inside the operating system.

source.title: Change instance termination protection

cards.statement: A responder can end tracked EC2 connections immediately by replacing the instance's security groups.
cards.explanation: Changing an EC2 instance's security groups leaves existing tracked connections active until they time out. Quarantine rules therefore need a separate way to end those connections.
cards.misconception: Attaching isolation security groups immediately breaks established tracked connections.

source.title: Amazon EC2 security group connection tracking

cards.statement: Deactivating an IAM user's access key automatically revokes sessions already created with that key.
cards.explanation: Deactivating a long-term access key leaves previously issued temporary credentials usable. Responders need to revoke those sessions separately to contain that access.
cards.misconception: Disabling a compromised access key also invalidates temporary credentials acquired with it.

source.title: AWS Security Incident Response Guide: Technique and access containment

cards.statement: IAM's role-session revocation policy denies requests from sessions issued before its configured cutoff.
cards.explanation: The IAM role-session revocation policy uses an explicit Deny with aws:TokenIssueTime earlier than a timestamp. Sessions created after that cutoff fall outside this Deny.

source.title: Revoke IAM role temporary security credentials

cards.statement: CloudTrail uses the same sharedEventID for records of one AWS action delivered to different accounts.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail records with matching sharedEventID values describe the same action across accounts. This helps responders correlate caller-side and resource-owner evidence.

source.title: CloudTrail record contents for management, data, and network activity events

cards.statement: CloudTrail's responseElements value of null proves that a recorded read-only API request fails.
cards.explanation: CloudTrail records null responseElements for read-only APIs, including successful requests. That field alone is insufficient evidence of API failure.
cards.misconception: A missing response payload means the recorded request failed.

source.title: CloudTrail record contents for management, data, and network activity events

cards.statement: Amazon Detective can automatically group findings involving the same IAM role sessions for investigation.
cards.explanation: Detective uses relationships such as shared role sessions to connect findings and entities. Responders use the group to investigate activity across the involved resources.

source.title: Analyzing finding groups

cards.statement: An Amazon GuardDuty Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile finding proves that the detected malware runs on the instance.
cards.explanation: Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile reports malicious files found by a disk scan. The finding establishes their presence, rather than proving that the instance executed them.
cards.misconception: The Execution prefix on a malware scan finding proves execution of the detected file.

source.title: Malware Protection for EC2 finding types

cards.statement: A responder's live artifact collection on an Amazon EC2 instance can change evidence on that instance.
cards.explanation: Running collection tools on a live EC2 system changes system data and artifacts. Responders document these changes when assessing the integrity of the evidence.

source.title: AWS Security Incident Response Guide: Collect and analyze forensic evidence

cards.statement: Amazon EBS lets a responder preserve disk evidence at request time while snapshot transfer continues.
cards.explanation: EBS snapshots preserve volume data as it exists when requested. Writes made while the snapshot transfers to Amazon S3 leave that captured disk evidence unchanged.

source.title: Create Amazon EBS snapshots

cards.statement: AWS WAF continues evaluating later web ACL rules after a matching rule uses the Count action.
cards.explanation: AWS WAF's Count action records a match and leaves the final allow-or-block decision to subsequent web ACL evaluation.

source.title: Using rule actions in AWS WAF

cards.statement: AWS WAF can enforce a rate-based rule as a precise cap on requests in its evaluation window.
cards.explanation: AWS WAF estimates request rates and applies rate limiting near the configured threshold. Its rate-based rules do not guarantee an exact request-rate cap.
cards.misconception: Rate-based rules enforce an exact request-rate ceiling.

source.title: Rate-based rule caveats in AWS WAF

cards.statement: AWS WAF uses a configured forwarded IP header for geo match evaluation.
cards.explanation: An AWS WAF geo match rule configured for forwarded IPs derives location from the first IP address in the specified request header. This changes which address the location check evaluates.

source.title: Geographic match rule statement

cards.statement: For CloudFront requests, AWS WAF can match a JA3 fingerprint across changes in source IP address.
cards.explanation: JA3 reflects a client's TLS configuration. An AWS WAF fingerprint rule can keep matching that configuration as its source IP address changes.

source.title: Reduce risks of user sign-up fraud and SMS pumping with Amazon Cognito user pools

cards.statement: AWS WAF's Continue oversize setting extends body inspection beyond the configured size limit.
cards.explanation: With Continue oversize handling, AWS WAF inspects the body content within the inspection limit. Extra body bytes remain outside that rule's inspection.
cards.misconception: Continue causes AWS WAF to inspect body bytes beyond the inspection limit.

source.title: Oversize web request components in AWS WAF

cards.statement: AWS WAF's Count return override lets a group evaluate rules after its first matching Block rule.
cards.explanation: A rule group's Count return override changes its result at the web ACL level. The first matching terminating rule still stops evaluation inside the group.
cards.misconception: A Count override of the group's returned action converts its internal blocking rules to non-terminating rules.

source.title: Overriding rule group actions in AWS WAF

cards.statement: An unhealthy associated Route 53 check can lower Shield Advanced's mitigation threshold for an Elastic IP.
cards.explanation: Shield Advanced uses associated Route 53 health checks to adjust attack sensitivity for protected Elastic IP addresses. An unhealthy check permits mitigation at lower thresholds.

source.title: Health-based detection using health checks with Shield Advanced and Route 53

cards.statement: Amazon CloudFront automatically interrupts an active download when its signed URL reaches expiration.
cards.explanation: CloudFront checks signed URL expiration when the HTTP request starts. A download that begins before expiration can complete after expiration on the existing connection.
cards.misconception: Signed URL expiration cuts off a download already underway.

source.title: Use signed URLs

cards.statement: Amazon CloudFront can assign native geographic restrictions to individual cache behaviors.
cards.explanation: CloudFront's native geographic restriction setting applies at the distribution level. Different restrictions for content subsets require a different control or separate distributions.
cards.misconception: Native geographic restrictions are configured per cache behavior.

source.title: Restrict the geographic distribution of your content

cards.statement: An Amazon S3 CORS rule directly grants object read permission to callers from its AllowedOrigins.
cards.explanation: Amazon S3 CORS rules control cross-origin browser behavior. Bucket policies and ACLs still determine object access permission when CORS is enabled.
cards.misconception: An allowed CORS origin receives S3 object permissions from the CORS rule.

source.title: Using cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)

cards.statement: An origin that validates Amazon CloudFront's secret custom header can reject requests that bypass CloudFront.
cards.explanation: CloudFront adds the configured custom header to origin requests. An origin that enforces its secret value can reject direct requests that lack this credential.

source.title: Restrict access to files

cards.statement: For non-exclusive association, AWS IoT Core requires MQTT client IDs to match thing names for thing policy variables.
cards.explanation: With non-exclusive thing association, AWS IoT Core uses the MQTT client ID to identify the thing for policy-variable evaluation. The client ID must match that thing's registered name.

source.title: Thing policy variables

cards.statement: EC2 Image Builder runs a configured security test workflow before distributing the generated image.
cards.explanation: When a pipeline includes a test workflow, Image Builder runs the test stage before beginning image distribution.

source.title: Manage build, test, and distribution workflows for Image Builder images

cards.statement: Amazon ECS can vend temporary task execution role credentials directly to application containers.
cards.explanation: Amazon ECS supplies task execution role credentials to its agents. Application containers do not receive those credentials directly.
cards.misconception: Amazon ECS delivers execution-role credentials to the application containers.

source.title: Amazon ECS task execution IAM role

cards.statement: Distinct Amazon ECS task roles create a security boundary between tasks on the same EC2 instance.
cards.explanation: On EC2, task roles do not create container isolation. A container may access credentials belonging to co-located tasks unless additional controls block that access.
cards.misconception: Assigning different task roles supplies a security isolation boundary on a shared EC2 host.

source.title: Amazon ECS task IAM role

cards.statement: In hybrid mode, Amazon Inspector can obtain eligible unmanaged EC2 instances' inventory from Amazon EBS snapshots.
cards.explanation: For eligible instances lacking usable SSM inventory, Inspector's agentless method extracts package inventory from EBS snapshots.

source.title: Scanning Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Inspector

cards.statement: With continuous scanning, Amazon Inspector rescans eligible ECR images when it adds a relevant CVE.
cards.explanation: A newly added vulnerability can change the assessment of an existing image. Inspector's continuous scanning refreshes findings for images within the configured coverage period.

source.title: Scanning Amazon Elastic Container Registry container images with Amazon Inspector

cards.statement: Amazon Inspector Lambda standard scanning can detect vulnerabilities in custom application source code.
cards.explanation: Lambda standard scanning checks dependencies for package vulnerabilities. Lambda code scanning assesses vulnerabilities in custom application code.
cards.misconception: Lambda standard scanning covers custom source-code vulnerabilities.

source.title: Scanning AWS Lambda functions with Amazon Inspector

cards.statement: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring can inspect process execution through a security agent on supported workloads.
cards.explanation: The GuardDuty security agent supplies runtime behavior that includes process execution, expanding visibility into activity within a workload.

source.title: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring

cards.statement: Session Manager can record commands executed through an SSH tunnel in its session logs.
cards.explanation: Session Manager serves as a tunnel for SSH and cannot log the commands inside that encrypted session; the command transcript is unavailable from its session logging.
cards.misconception: Enabling Session Manager session logging records commands inside tunneled SSH connections.

source.title: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager

cards.statement: For direct SSH connections, EC2 Instance Connect requires a network path from the client to the instance.
cards.explanation: EC2 Instance Connect supplies SSH authentication by delivering a public key. The client still needs network reachability to the instance for a direct SSH connection.

source.title: Connect to a Linux instance using EC2 Instance Connect

cards.statement: AWS-RunPatchBaseline marks a managed node compliant when its Scan operation completes successfully.
cards.explanation: Scan reports the managed node's patch state. A successful Scan can report missing approved patches; it leaves their installation to an Install operation.
cards.misconception: A successful patch scan establishes that the node meets its patch baseline.

source.title: SSM Command document for patching: AWS-RunPatchBaseline

cards.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can apply a denied-topic policy to user inputs and model responses.
cards.explanation: A configured denied-topic filter evaluates the topics in a user's query and the model's response, helping enforce the application's subject-area restrictions.

source.title: Detect and filter harmful content by using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

cards.statement: ApplyGuardrail runs the application's foundation model as part of checking supplied text against a guardrail.
cards.explanation: ApplyGuardrail assesses supplied text separately from model inference. An application can request that assessment before it invokes a foundation model.
cards.misconception: ApplyGuardrail invokes the application's foundation model during guardrail assessment.

source.title: Use the ApplyGuardrail API in your application

cards.statement: An Amazon EC2 security group reference permits instance traffic across subnets through a routed middlebox.
cards.explanation: Across a middlebox route, instance security groups need the other instance's private IP or subnet CIDR as the source. Referencing its security group does not authorize that path.
cards.misconception: Security group references authorize the source instance even when a middlebox sits on the route.

source.title: Security group rules

cards.statement: An Amazon VPC network ACL can block an EC2 instance's DNS queries to the VPC's AmazonProvidedDNS address.
cards.explanation: Amazon VPC exempts its AmazonProvidedDNS resolver traffic from network ACL filtering, even when a matching deny rule exists.
cards.misconception: A subnet network ACL applies its deny rules to queries sent to the Amazon-provided resolver.

source.title: Control subnet traffic with network access control lists

cards.statement: AWS Network Firewall still applies its stateful rules to packets that match a stateless Pass action.
cards.explanation: A stateless Pass action ends packet inspection in AWS Network Firewall. Forward to stateful rules is the action that sends a packet onward for stateful inspection.
cards.misconception: Passing stateless inspection still subjects a packet to the stateful rule engine.

source.title: Defining rule actions in AWS Network Firewall

cards.statement: With strict rule order, AWS Network Firewall's Drop established default permits TCP connection handshakes.
cards.explanation: The AWS Network Firewall Drop established default lets TCP establish a connection before deciding on application traffic. This makes application-layer pass rules usable in a default-deny policy.

source.title: Managing evaluation order for Suricata compatible rules in AWS Network Firewall

cards.statement: For inter-VPC flows on one AWS Transit Gateway, appliance mode automatically pins both directions to one inspection AZ.
cards.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway appliance mode pins an inspection VPC attachment to the chosen Availability Zone for a flow, preserving the return path for stateful inspection.

source.title: How AWS Transit Gateway works

cards.statement: Network Access Analyzer can confirm that an attacker has sent packets along a path reported in a finding.
cards.explanation: Network Access Analyzer infers possible paths from network configuration. Its findings show configured exposure, rather than observed packet traffic.
cards.misconception: A finding from configuration analysis proves that traffic actually traversed the reported path.

source.title: How Network Access Analyzer works

cards.statement: Route 53 Resolver returns SERVFAIL by default when an associated DNS Firewall fails to answer a query.
cards.explanation: The default DNS Firewall failure policy blocks queries whose firewall evaluation times out. Route 53 Resolver returns SERVFAIL, preserving enforcement during an outage.

source.title: DNS Firewall VPC configuration

cards.statement: Engineers can isolate AWS Transit Gateway segments by propagating VPC routes into selected route tables.
cards.explanation: Transit gateway route propagation installs a VPC's CIDRs into chosen route tables. A segment learns those routes through the table its attachment uses.

source.title: How AWS Transit Gateway works

cards.statement: Adding an AWS Client VPN route automatically authorizes authenticated clients to reach its destination.
cards.explanation: AWS Client VPN route tables choose network paths. Separate authorization rules determine which authenticated clients may reach a destination network.
cards.misconception: A Client VPN route also grants destination access to authenticated clients.

source.title: AWS Client VPN routes

cards.statement: With group and endpoint policies defined, AWS Verified Access requires both policy documents to allow a request.
cards.explanation: An endpoint policy adds an access gate to the group policy. AWS Verified Access grants a request when both configured policy documents allow it.

source.title: Verified Access policy evaluation

cards.statement: AWS Network Firewall automatically redirects subnet traffic through a firewall endpoint when engineers create it.
cards.explanation: Engineers insert AWS Network Firewall endpoints into traffic paths by updating VPC routes. Creating an endpoint leaves existing routes in place.
cards.misconception: Creating a firewall endpoint automatically puts it into the subnet's existing traffic path.

source.title: VPC route table configuration for AWS Network Firewall

cards.statement: On scheduled secret deletion, AWS Direct Connect changes must_encrypt to should_encrypt after removing the last CKN.
cards.explanation: When scheduled secret deletion leads AWS Direct Connect to disassociate a connection's final CKN, the service changes must_encrypt to should_encrypt to avoid sudden packet loss.
cards.volatilityNote: AWS may revise its automatic response to deletion of the final MACsec key.

source.title: MAC Security in Direct Connect
